entries.title: Birth of the eval — flow de-bloat and the harness land in the same commit
entries.what: c84aff31 does two things at once: it guts the v2 directive stack (execute.directive.xml -667 lines, critic.directive.xml -482, phase-execution-protocol.directive.xml -351, critic-protocol -279, infra/interface -190/-182) AND introduces ai/flow-eval/ from scratch (cli.ts, runner.ts, provision.ts, evidence.ts, judge.ts, observer.ts, prompts.ts, types.ts, scenarios.json, README.md, harness.test.ts). The eval was built to prove empirically that the flow itself — not the model — was choking on ceremony. Docs added same day (7e499b7b, RUNBOOK.ru.md) narrate this as 'intellectual eval harness'. The harness runs a real cheap model (initially openai/gpt-5.6-luna, later locked to llm-proxy/deepseek-v4-flash) against an isolated sandbox, observed by a bounded external observer, scored by a stochastic LLM judge AND deterministic sdd-check/sdd-verify mechanics.

impact.why: Founding commit: cuts the v2 directive stack and introduces the eval harness in the same commit — there is no 'before the harness' run to pair it against; the harness's value is proven by every later entry that used it (PROGRESS-REPORT.md TL;DR: clean authoring 1/4→5/6, scaffold tool-load 45→24-33, over the whole arc that follows).

entries.title: H2 — write-first token reduction on authoring: tokens down, cleanliness not up (orthogonal, unmerged)
entries.what: N=2/arm A/B on the authoring phase: baseline (read-heavy) vs write-first treatment, run on two parallel worktree tracks (:4098/:4099) sharing one dist. Headline finding: less reading does cut tokens sharply (input 83k→49k, −41%) but does NOT improve authoring cleanliness (treatment 0/2 clean vs baseline 1/2 clean) — tokens and quality proved orthogonal on this axis. This is the reason later work moved 'reduce reading' to lazy-loading at the tool/directive-assembly level instead of prompt wording (reinforced independently by H3's negative wording-A/B result three days later).

entries.title: H4/H5/B2 — recover code->spec: router-chain kills it, direct process saves it
entries.what: The brownfield 'recover a lost spec from code' branch degenerated on the cheap model: baseline (V1, full greenfield-authoring ceremony) never wrote a spec in 20 messages, reasoning ballooned to 68249 tokens. Diagnosis via a saved transcript showed the agent reading root.directive.xml -> scope.directive.xml -> router.directive.xml (22 tool calls, artifact=none). V2 (direct: read code -> list behaviour -> one Write, explicit ban on reading the router/directive chain) fixed it outright.

entries.title: B4 — 10-variation isolation of the recover degrader
entries.what: 8-10 isolating prompt variations pinned down exactly what breaks recover: router/directive-CHAIN is fatal (V1, V3 both FAIL with no artifact); discovery/interview in headless mode is not fatal but x4 more expensive (V4); missing explicit steps/structure is x4 more expensive (V8, 43639 tokens); a single SKILL.md read, a few-shot example, or verbosity are all near-noise (V5/V6/V7). Optimum (direct + explicit steps + no router-chain + no discovery) reproduced 3x (V2/V9/V10, ~10-10.8k tokens, reason 334-514).

entries.title: C — keepers locked at N=3
entries.what: H9+H10+H11 combined ran three times on the ladder at the 300s budget (H9-run, keepers#1, keepers#2). Every run reached FLOW_VERSION=v2 (migration PASS) on all three tiers (portal/scope/module); module occasionally worker-errors at 300s after already flipping to v2 (grade still PASS). Consistent across N=3 → keepers statistically locked; no 4th run needed.
entries.diff_before: N=1 (single ladder run per keeper)
entries.diff_after: N=3, all-tiers-v2 in every run

impact.why: Three independent 300s runs all reach v2 on every tier — the keeper set is reproducible, not a single-run fluke.
impact.d_trajectory: portal ~38-49, scope ~38-60, module ~55-66 tools across runs

entries.title: B1 — de-ceremony the execute prompt (KEEPER)
entries.what: Second optimization surface: the execute/closure flow (not migration). Baseline node slugify run reached DONE but spent 43 tools orienting before the first write (read x33) plus task x4 + skill x2 — the agent walked the router/skill chain because PHASE_PROMPTS.execute literally instructed reading SKILL.md + router.directive.xml. Mutation: go straight to execute.directive.xml (+ phase-execution-protocol), skip the chain, name the closure spine explicitly (verify, close round, group audit+review receipts), done = ticket DONE with receipts. Same de-ceremony lever proven on migration.
entries.diff_before: Read and follow the installed SDD skill and router/directive chain (SKILL.md + router.directive.xml)
entries.diff_after: Go straight to execute.directive.xml; do NOT traverse the router/skill chain; closure spine + done-oracle named

impact.why: Full lifecycle to DONE preserved (R-COMPLETE pass) while cost dropped sharply — the router/skill chain-walk was pure orientation overhead the phase does not need.
impact.d_trajectory: orientation 43 → 22 tools; router/skill traversal task4/skill2 → 0/0; total 65 → 60
